title: Ch 8 · Model of Matter - Atoms and Molecules

questions.q: The simplest unit of an element is
questions.explain: An atom is the simplest unit of an element. An element is made up of only one type of atom.
questions.lo: Describe an atom as the simplest unit of an element

notes.0: A mixture contains two or more substances that are not chemically combined. It is not a single unit at all.
notes.1: A compound contains two or more elements chemically combined. It is made of smaller units, so it cannot be the simplest.
notes.2: A molecule is made of two or more atoms chemically combined. Think about the smaller unit that molecules are built from.

questions.q: A sample of the element carbon is made up of
questions.explain: An element is made up of only one type of atom. A sample of carbon contains only carbon atoms.
questions.lo: Describe an atom as the simplest unit of an element

notes.0: Carbon dioxide is a compound of carbon and oxygen. A sample of an element contains no other elements.
notes.1: Hydrogen is a different element. A sample of an element contains only one type of atom.
notes.3: Atoms of many different elements would make a mixture or a compound. An element contains only one type of atom.

why.right: A sample of carbon contains only carbon atoms because an element is made up of one type of atom.
wrong: A sample of carbon contains only carbon atoms because carbon atoms push all other atoms away.
A sample of carbon contains only carbon atoms because carbon atoms are the only atoms found in solids.

questions.q: Why can an atom not be seen with the naked eye?
questions.explain: An atom is extremely tiny, far smaller than anything the naked eye can see. About a million carbon atoms in a row span only the width of a strand of hair.
questions.lo: Compare the size of an atom with the sizes of everyday objects

notes.0: Charge has nothing to do with whether something can be seen. Think about how big an atom is.
notes.2: Even atoms in a solid, which only vibrate, cannot be seen. Their speed is not the reason.
notes.3: Atoms do have mass. Think about how big an atom is compared with things we can see.

why.right: An atom cannot be seen with the naked eye because it is far too tiny for eyes to see.
wrong: An atom cannot be seen with the naked eye because it moves far too quickly for eyes to follow.
An atom cannot be seen with the naked eye because it is always hidden inside a larger molecule.

questions.q: About 1 million carbon atoms in a row span the width of a
questions.explain: Atoms are extremely tiny. About 1 million carbon atoms placed in a row would span only the width of a strand of human hair.
questions.lo: Compare the size of an atom with the sizes of everyday objects

notes.1: A fingernail is far wider than a million atoms. A million atoms in a row is still a very short distance.
notes.2: A football stadium is enormous compared with a million atoms. A million atoms in a row is still a very short distance.
notes.3: A grain of rice is much wider than a million atoms. Think of something even thinner that is still just visible.

questions.q: Which list is in order of increasing size?
choices: atom, strand of hair, grain of rice
strand of hair, atom, grain of rice
atom, grain of rice, strand of hair
grain of rice, atom, strand of hair
questions.explain: An atom is the smallest of the three and cannot be seen. A strand of hair is very thin, and a grain of rice is wider than a hair.
questions.lo: Compare the size of an atom with the sizes of everyday objects

notes.1: An atom is far smaller than a strand of hair. A strand of hair is about a million atoms wide.
notes.2: A strand of hair is thinner than a grain of rice. Compare the widths of the two everyday objects.
notes.3: A list in order of increasing size starts with the smallest. A grain of rice is not smaller than an atom.

why.right: The order atom, hair strand, rice grain is increasing size because a hair is a million atoms wide and thinner than rice.
wrong: The order atom, hair strand, rice grain is increasing size because an atom is about as wide as a hair.
The order atom, hair strand, rice grain is increasing size because a rice grain contains fewer atoms than a hair.

questions.q: Which sub-atomic particle has a negative charge?
questions.explain: The electron has a negative charge of −1. The proton has a positive charge and the neutron has no charge.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: A proton has a positive charge. The question asks for the negative particle.
notes.2: A neutron has no charge at all. The question asks for the negative particle.

questions.q: Which sub-atomic particle has no charge?
questions.explain: The neutron has no charge, so it is neutral. The proton is positive and the electron is negative.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: An electron has a negative charge. Think about which particle's name suggests it is neutral.
notes.1: A proton has a positive charge. Think about which particle's name suggests it is neutral.

questions.q: The nucleus of an atom is made up of
questions.explain: The nucleus is at the centre of the atom and contains protons and neutrons. Electrons move around outside the nucleus.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: Protons are in the nucleus, but electrons move around outside it.
notes.1: Electrons are not in the nucleus. They move around outside it.
notes.2: Neutrons are in the nucleus, but electrons move around outside it.

questions.q: Where are electrons found in an atom?
questions.explain: Electrons move around the nucleus, outside it. The nucleus contains only protons and neutrons.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.1: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons only. Electrons are found elsewhere in the atom.
notes.2: Neutrons are in the nucleus, and electrons are not joined to them. Electrons are found elsewhere in the atom.
notes.3: Electrons are separate particles and are not inside protons. Think about where electrons are found compared with the nucleus.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of an electron?
questions.explain: An electron has a relative charge of −1. A proton has a relative charge of +1, and a neutron has 0.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: None of the three sub-atomic particles has a charge of +2. The electron is a negative particle.
notes.1: A charge of +1 belongs to the proton. The electron has the opposite type of charge.
notes.3: A charge of 0 belongs to the neutron. The electron is a charged particle.

questions.q: What is the relative mass of a proton?
questions.explain: A proton has a relative mass of 1. A neutron also has a relative mass of 1, and an electron has a relative mass of almost zero.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: A value of −1 is the relative charge of an electron, not a mass. Mass cannot be negative.
notes.1: A proton has mass. It is one of the two heavy particles in the nucleus.
notes.2: Almost zero is the relative mass of the electron. The proton is much heavier.

questions.q: A particle is in the nucleus and has a charge of +1. It is
questions.explain: A particle in the nucleus with a charge of +1 is a proton. The neutron is also in the nucleus but has no charge.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: A molecule is a group of atoms, not a particle inside an atom. The particle described is inside the nucleus.
notes.2: A neutron is in the nucleus but has no charge. This particle has a charge of +1.
notes.3: An electron moves around outside the nucleus and has a charge of −1. This particle is in the nucleus with a positive charge.

why.right: A positive particle in the nucleus is a proton, because protons have a relative charge of +1.
wrong: A positive particle in the nucleus is a proton, because protons are the lightest particles in the atom.
A positive particle in the nucleus is a proton, because protons move around the outside of the nucleus.

questions.q: A particle has a relative mass of 1 and no charge. It is
questions.explain: A neutron has a relative mass of 1 and no charge. A proton also has a relative mass of 1 but has a charge of +1.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.0: An electron has a charge of −1 and almost zero mass. This particle has no charge and a relative mass of 1.
notes.2: A proton has a relative mass of 1 but carries a charge of +1. This particle has no charge.

why.right: A particle with a relative mass of 1 and no charge is a neutron, because neutrons are neutral.
wrong: A particle with a relative mass of 1 and no charge is a neutron, because neutrons move around the nucleus.
A particle with a relative mass of 1 and no charge is a neutron, because neutrons are lighter than electrons.

questions.q: A particle moves around the nucleus and has a charge of −1. It is
questions.explain: A particle that moves around the nucleus with a charge of −1 is an electron. Protons and neutrons are both inside the nucleus.
questions.lo: Identify a sub-atomic particle from its charge, mass and position

notes.1: A proton has a charge of +1 and is inside the nucleus. This particle is negative and outside the nucleus.
notes.2: A neutron has no charge and is inside the nucleus. This particle is negative and outside the nucleus.

why.right: A negative particle moving around the nucleus is an electron, because electrons have a relative charge of −1.
wrong: A negative particle moving around the nucleus is an electron, because electrons are the heaviest particles in an atom.
A negative particle moving around the nucleus is an electron, because electrons are made of protons and neutrons.

questions.q: An atom is electrically neutral because it has equal numbers of
questions.explain: Each proton has a charge of +1 and each electron has a charge of −1. Equal numbers of protons and electrons cancel out, so the atom has no overall charge.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: Neutrons have no charge, so they cannot cancel the charge of protons. Think about which particle has the opposite charge to a proton.
notes.1: Neutrons have no charge, so their number does not affect the overall charge. Think about which particles carry charge.
notes.3: Atoms and molecules are not sub-atomic particles. Neutrality depends on the charged particles inside an atom.

why.right: An atom is neutral because the positive charges of its protons cancel the negative charges of its electrons.
wrong: An atom is neutral because its neutrons soak up the charges of its protons and electrons.
An atom is neutral because its electrons are inside the nucleus with the protons.

questions.q: A lithium atom has 4 neutrons. Why do they not affect its charge?
questions.explain: Neutrons have no charge. Adding or removing neutrons does not change the overall charge of the lithium atom.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: Neutrons do have mass, with a relative mass of 1. Their effect on charge depends on something else.
notes.1: Neutrons do not move around the nucleus. They are inside it, and their position is not the reason.
notes.2: Neutrons are inside the nucleus, not outside it. Think about whether neutrons carry any charge.

why.right: Neutrons do not change an atom's charge because each neutron has a relative charge of zero.
wrong: Neutrons do not change an atom's charge because each neutron has a relative mass of zero.
Neutrons do not change an atom's charge because each neutron cancels out one electron.

questions.q: An oxygen atom has 8 protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: An atom is electrically neutral, so it has the same number of electrons as protons. An oxygen atom with 8 protons has 8 electrons.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: Halving the number of protons does not give the number of electrons. A neutral atom needs its positive and negative charges to balance.
notes.1: Doubling the number of protons does not give the number of electrons. A neutral atom needs its positive and negative charges to balance.
notes.2: An atom with protons must also have electrons to balance their charge. Otherwise the atom would be positive.

why.right: An oxygen atom with 8 protons has 8 electrons because a neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
wrong: An oxygen atom with 8 protons has 8 electrons because electrons always equal the number of neutrons.
An oxygen atom with 8 protons has 8 electrons because every atom has exactly 8 electrons.

questions.q: A sodium atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. A sodium atom with 11 protons has 11 electrons. The 12 neutrons have no charge and do not count.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.1: 12 is the number of neutrons. Neutrons have no charge, so they do not decide the number of electrons.
notes.2: 23 is the protons and neutrons added together. Only the charged particles need to balance in a neutral atom.
notes.3: 1 is the difference between neutrons and protons. A neutral atom needs its positive and negative charges to balance.

why.right: A sodium atom with 11 protons has 11 electrons because the protons and electrons must balance in charge.
wrong: A sodium atom with 11 protons has 11 electrons because electrons always number one less than neutrons.
A sodium atom with 11 protons has 11 electrons because every metal atom has 11 electrons.

questions.q: A carbon atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. A carbon atom with 6 protons has 6 electrons. The neutrons have no charge and do not count.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: 14 is the protons and neutrons added together. Only the charged particles need to balance in a neutral atom.
notes.1: 2 is the difference between neutrons and protons. A neutral atom needs its positive and negative charges to balance.
notes.3: 8 is the number of neutrons. Neutrons have no charge, so they do not decide the number of electrons.

why.right: A carbon atom with 6 protons has 6 electrons because the protons and electrons must balance in charge.
wrong: A carbon atom with 6 protons has 6 electrons because each electron is paired with one neutron.
A carbon atom with 6 protons has 6 electrons because electrons are found inside the nucleus with protons.

questions.q: An atom has 13 electrons. How many protons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. An atom with 13 electrons has 13 protons.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: Doubling the number of electrons does not give the number of protons. A neutral atom needs its positive and negative charges to balance.
notes.2: An atom with electrons must also have protons to balance their charge. Otherwise the atom would be negative.
notes.3: One more proton than electrons would give the atom an overall positive charge. Think about which numbers must match.

why.right: An atom with 13 electrons has 13 protons because the protons and electrons must balance in charge.
wrong: An atom with 13 electrons has 13 protons because protons and electrons have the same mass.
An atom with 13 electrons has 13 protons because each electron sits inside one proton.

questions.q: A helium atom has 2 protons and 2 electrons. What is its overall charge?
questions.explain: The 2 protons give +2 and the 2 electrons give −2. These cancel out, so the overall charge of the helium atom is 0.
questions.lo: Use the electrical neutrality of an atom to find numbers of protons and electrons

notes.0: Only the electrons were counted. The protons also carry charge, which must be included.
notes.2: Protons and electrons have opposite charges, so their charges cancel rather than add up. Counting them all as positive is the mistake.
notes.3: Only the protons were counted. The electrons also carry charge, which must be included.

why.right: A helium atom with 2 protons and 2 electrons is neutral because +2 and −2 cancel out.
wrong: A helium atom with 2 protons and 2 electrons is neutral because helium is a gas and gases have no charge.
A helium atom with 2 protons and 2 electrons is neutral because protons and electrons both have no charge.

questions.q: Carbon atoms have 6 protons and 6, 7 or 8 neutrons. This shows the number of neutrons
choices: always equals the number of protons
can differ from the number of protons
always equals the number of electrons
questions.explain: All carbon atoms have 6 protons, but they can have 6, 7 or 8 neutrons. So the number of neutrons can differ from the number of protons.
questions.lo: State that the number of neutrons in an atom need not equal the number of protons

notes.0: These atoms have different numbers of neutrons but are all carbon. The number of neutrons does not decide the element.
notes.1: Carbon atoms with 7 or 8 neutrons do not have equal numbers of protons and neutrons. Look again at the numbers given.
notes.3: Carbon atoms have 6 electrons, but some have 7 or 8 neutrons. Look again at the numbers given.

why.right: Carbon atoms can have 6, 7 or 8 neutrons because only the number of protons, which stays at 6, decides the element.
wrong: Carbon atoms can have 6, 7 or 8 neutrons because the number of protons also changes to match.
Carbon atoms can have 6, 7 or 8 neutrons because neutrons carry a charge that balances extra electrons.

questions.q: The mass of an atom is mainly the mass of its
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus, and each has a relative mass of 1. Electrons have almost no mass, so nearly all of an atom's mass is in its nucleus.
questions.lo: Recognise that the mass of an atom is mainly the mass of its nucleus

notes.0: Empty space has no mass. Think about where the heavy particles in an atom are found.
notes.1: Electrons have a relative mass of almost zero. Think about where the heavy particles in an atom are found.
notes.2: The pathways of electrons are not objects with mass. Think about where the heavy particles in an atom are found.

why.right: An atom's mass is mainly in its nucleus because protons and neutrons are far heavier than electrons.
wrong: An atom's mass is mainly in its nucleus because the nucleus is the largest part of the atom.
An atom's mass is mainly in its nucleus because the nucleus contains all of the atom's electrons.

questions.q: Why is the mass of electrons in an atom considered negligible?
choices: they are much lighter than protons and neutrons
questions.explain: An electron has a relative mass of almost zero, while protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1. Electrons add very little to the mass of an atom.
questions.lo: Recognise that the mass of an atom is mainly the mass of its nucleus

notes.1: Being outside the nucleus does not decide how heavy a particle is. Compare the relative masses of the three particles.
notes.2: Charge and mass are different properties. Compare the relative masses of the three particles.
notes.3: Speed does not change how much mass a particle has. Compare the relative masses of the three particles.

why.right: Electron mass in an atom is negligible because each electron is far lighter than a proton or neutron.
wrong: Electron mass in an atom is negligible because the negative charge of each electron cancels out its mass.
Electron mass in an atom is negligible because particles that move very fast have no mass.

questions.q: An atom has 6 protons, 6 neutrons and 6 electrons. Which particles give most of its mass?
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1. Electrons have almost no mass, so the 6 protons and 6 neutrons give most of the mass.
questions.lo: Recognise that the mass of an atom is mainly the mass of its nucleus

notes.1: Electrons have a relative mass of almost zero. Only one of these two particles adds much mass.
notes.2: Electrons have a relative mass of almost zero, so they add very little mass. Think about the particles in the nucleus.
notes.3: Electrons have a relative mass of almost zero. Only one of these two particles adds much mass.

why.right: Protons and neutrons give most of an atom's mass because each has a relative mass of 1.
wrong: Protons and neutrons give most of an atom's mass because they carry all of the atom's charge.
Protons and neutrons give most of an atom's mass because they move faster than electrons.

questions.q: In the periodic table, the number above an element's symbol shows the number of
choices: atoms in one of its molecules
neutrons in one of its atoms
protons in one of its atoms
questions.explain: The number above an element's symbol is the number of protons in one of its atoms. Each element has its own number of protons.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Many elements do not form molecules at all. The number above the symbol is about a particle inside each atom.
notes.1: The number of neutrons can differ between atoms of the same element. The number above the symbol is the same for every atom of that element.
notes.3: The number of molecules depends on how much of the element there is. The number above the symbol is about a particle inside each atom.

questions.q: Elements in the periodic table are arranged in order of increasing
questions.explain: Elements in the periodic table are arranged in order of increasing number of protons. Each element has one more proton than the element before it.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Atom size does not rise steadily across the periodic table. The order follows a number that identifies each element.
notes.2: Atoms of the same element can have different numbers of neutrons. The order follows a number that is the same for every atom of an element.
notes.3: Many elements do not form molecules. The order follows a number found inside every atom of an element.

why.right: The periodic table follows proton number because each element has its own fixed number of protons.
wrong: The periodic table follows proton number because protons are the only particles that have mass.
The periodic table follows proton number because all atoms of an element have the same number of neutrons.

questions.q: What makes the atoms of one element different from another element?
questions.explain: Every element has its own number of protons in its atoms. Atoms of different elements have different numbers of protons.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Electrons in all atoms move around the nucleus. Their speed does not decide which element an atom belongs to.
notes.1: Atoms of the same element can have different numbers of neutrons. So neutrons cannot be what sets elements apart.
notes.2: Single atoms have no colour. The colour of a substance does not decide which element its atoms are.

why.right: Atoms of different elements differ because each element has its own fixed number of protons.
wrong: Atoms of different elements differ because each element has its own fixed number of neutrons.
Atoms of different elements differ because each element's electrons move at their own speed.

questions.q: Atom X has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Atom Y has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. They are
questions.explain: X and Y both have 6 protons, so they are atoms of the same element, carbon. They differ only in their number of neutrons, which does not change the element.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Neutrons have no charge, so a different number of neutrons does not change the charge. Both atoms are neutral.
notes.1: X and Y are single atoms, not groups of atoms combined. A molecule needs two or more atoms joined together.
notes.3: The number of neutrons does not decide the element. Compare the number of protons in X and Y.

why.right: Atoms with 6 protons each are the same element, because the number of protons decides the element.
wrong: Atoms with 6 protons each are the same element, because the number of neutrons decides the element.
Atoms with 6 protons each are the same element, because atoms of one element always have equal mass.

questions.q: Atom P has 7 protons. Atom Q has 8 protons. They are
questions.explain: P has 7 protons and Q has 8 protons. Atoms with different numbers of protons belong to different elements, which here are nitrogen and oxygen.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Atoms of the same element always have the same number of protons. P and Q have different numbers.
notes.1: P and Q are single atoms, not molecules. Their numbers of protons are also different.
notes.2: The question gives only the numbers of protons, which say nothing certain about mass. Think about what the number of protons tells us.

why.right: Atoms with 7 and 8 protons are different elements, because each element has its own number of protons.
wrong: Atoms with 7 and 8 protons are different elements, because each element has its own number of neutrons.
Atoms with 7 and 8 protons are different elements, because any two separate atoms are always different elements.

questions.q: An atom has 3 protons, 3 electrons and 4 neutrons. Which element is it?
questions.explain: The number of protons identifies the element. An atom with 3 protons is lithium. Hydrogen has 1 proton, helium has 2 and carbon has 6.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.0: Hydrogen atoms have only 1 proton. Use the number of protons, not the neutrons, to identify the element.
notes.2: Carbon atoms have 6 protons, which is double this atom's number. Use the number of protons to identify the element.
notes.3: Helium atoms have 2 protons. Use the number of protons to identify the element.

why.right: An atom with 3 protons is lithium because the element is found from the number of protons.
wrong: An atom with 3 protons is lithium because the element is found from the number of neutrons.
An atom with 3 protons is lithium because the element is found by adding protons and neutrons.

questions.q: An atom has 7 protons and 8 neutrons. Which element is it?
questions.explain: An atom with 7 protons is nitrogen. The number of neutrons does not decide the element.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.1: Lithium atoms have 3 protons. Use the number of protons to identify the element.
notes.2: Oxygen atoms have 8 protons. The 8 here is the number of neutrons, which does not decide the element.
notes.3: Carbon atoms have 6 protons. Use the number of protons to identify the element.

why.right: An atom with 7 protons and 8 neutrons is nitrogen because the element is found from the number of protons.
wrong: An atom with 7 protons and 8 neutrons is nitrogen because the element is found from the number of neutrons.
An atom with 7 protons and 8 neutrons is nitrogen because the element is found by adding protons and neutrons.

questions.q: A neutral atom has 2 electrons. Which element is it?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. An atom with 2 electrons has 2 protons, so it is helium.
questions.lo: Use the number of protons to identify an element

notes.1: Lithium atoms have 3 protons and so 3 electrons. This atom has 2 electrons.
notes.2: Carbon atoms have 6 protons and so 6 electrons. This atom has 2 electrons.
notes.3: Hydrogen atoms have 1 proton and so 1 electron. This atom has 2 electrons.

why.right: A neutral atom with 2 electrons is helium because it must also have 2 protons, which identify helium.
wrong: A neutral atom with 2 electrons is helium because the element is found from the number of neutrons.
A neutral atom with 2 electrons is helium because only atoms of gases have so few electrons.

questions.q: A molecule is made up of
choices: two or more substances mixed together
two or more atoms chemically combined
questions.explain: A molecule is made up of two or more atoms chemically combined. The atoms can be of the same element or of different elements.
questions.lo: State that a molecule is two or more atoms chemically combined

notes.0: A single atom on its own is not a molecule. A molecule needs atoms joined together.
notes.1: Substances mixed together form a mixture. In a molecule the parts are chemically joined.
notes.2: Protons and neutrons make up the nucleus of an atom. A molecule is built from whole atoms.

questions.q: Which formula represents a molecule?
questions.explain: H₂ shows two hydrogen atoms chemically combined, so it is a molecule. H, He and C each represent a single atom.
questions.lo: State that a molecule is two or more atoms chemically combined

notes.0: H stands for a single hydrogen atom. A molecule needs two or more atoms joined together.
notes.2: He is the symbol for helium, written with two letters. It stands for a single helium atom, not two atoms.
notes.3: C stands for a single carbon atom. A molecule needs two or more atoms joined together.

why.right: H₂ represents a molecule because the small 2 shows two hydrogen atoms chemically combined.
wrong: H₂ represents a molecule because hydrogen is a gas and all gases are made of molecules.
H₂ represents a molecule because the small 2 shows that hydrogen has two protons.

questions.q: A chemical formula shows the
choices: size of each atom in a molecule
colour of each atom in a molecule
types and numbers of atoms in a molecule
number of protons in each atom
questions.explain: A chemical formula uses symbols to show which types of atoms are in a molecule. The small numbers show how many atoms of each type there are.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: A formula does not show how big atoms are. It uses symbols and small numbers.
notes.1: Atoms have no colour, and a formula does not show colour. It uses symbols and small numbers.
notes.3: The number of protons is found from the periodic table, not the formula. The small numbers in a formula count something else.

questions.q: In H₂O, how many hydrogen atoms are there?
questions.explain: In H₂O, the small 2 after H shows two hydrogen atoms. The O has no number, so there is one oxygen atom.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: 3 is the total number of atoms in H₂O. The question asks only about hydrogen atoms.
notes.1: The small number after a symbol counts the atoms of that element. Look at the number written after H.
notes.3: The H in H₂O is the symbol for hydrogen, so there are hydrogen atoms. Look at the number written after H.

why.right: H₂O has two hydrogen atoms because the small 2 counts the atoms of the element just before it.
wrong: H₂O has two hydrogen atoms because the small 2 counts the atoms of the element just after it.
H₂O has two hydrogen atoms because the small 2 counts all the atoms in the molecule.

questions.q: In NH₃, how many hydrogen atoms are there?
questions.explain: In NH₃, the small 3 after H shows three hydrogen atoms. The N has no number, so there is one nitrogen atom.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.1: There is no 2 in NH₃. Look at the small number written after H.
notes.2: 1 is the number of nitrogen atoms, since N has no number after it. Look at the number written after H.
notes.3: 4 is the total number of atoms in NH₃. The question asks only about hydrogen atoms.

why.right: NH₃ has three hydrogen atoms because the small 3 counts the atoms of the element just before it.
wrong: NH₃ has three hydrogen atoms because the small 3 counts the atoms of the element at the start.
NH₃ has three hydrogen atoms because the small 3 counts all the atoms in the molecule.

questions.q: How many oxygen atoms are in one NO₂ molecule?
questions.explain: In NO₂, the small 2 after O shows two oxygen atoms. The N has no number, so there is one nitrogen atom.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: 1 is the number of nitrogen atoms. Look at the small number written after O.
notes.2: The O in NO₂ is the symbol for oxygen, so there are oxygen atoms. Look at the number written after O.
notes.3: 3 is the total number of atoms in NO₂. The question asks only about oxygen atoms.

why.right: NO₂ has two oxygen atoms because the small 2 counts the atoms of the element just before it.
wrong: NO₂ has two oxygen atoms because the small 2 counts the atoms of the element at the start.
NO₂ has two oxygen atoms because the small 2 counts all the atoms in the molecule.

questions.q: What is the total number of atoms in one CO₂ molecule?
questions.explain: CO₂ has 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms. The total number of atoms is 1 + 2 = 3.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: 1 is only the carbon atom. The oxygen atoms must be added too.
notes.1: 2 is only the oxygen atoms. The carbon atom must be added too.
notes.2: The small 2 applies only to oxygen, not to carbon. Count each type of atom, then add.

why.right: CO₂ has three atoms because C counts as one atom and the small 2 adds two oxygen atoms.
wrong: CO₂ has three atoms because C counts as one atom and the small 2 adds two carbon atoms.
CO₂ has three atoms because every molecule of a gas contains exactly three atoms.

questions.q: What is the total number of atoms in one CH₄ molecule?
questions.explain: CH₄ has 1 carbon atom and 4 hydrogen atoms. The total number of atoms is 1 + 4 = 5.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: 1 is only the carbon atom. The hydrogen atoms must be added too.
notes.2: 4 is only the hydrogen atoms. The carbon atom must be added too.
notes.3: 2 is the number of different types of atom. The question asks for the total number of atoms.

why.right: CH₄ has five atoms because C counts as one atom and the small 4 adds four hydrogen atoms.
wrong: CH₄ has five atoms because C counts as one atom and the small 4 adds four carbon atoms.
CH₄ has five atoms because every molecule containing carbon has exactly five atoms.

questions.q: Which types of atoms are in NH₃?
questions.explain: N is the symbol for nitrogen and H is the symbol for hydrogen. NH₃ contains nitrogen atoms and hydrogen atoms.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.1: NH₃ contains a second symbol, H, after the N. Each different symbol stands for a different type of atom.
notes.2: The symbol for sodium is Na, not N. Check what N stands for.
notes.3: The symbol for helium is He, not H. Check what H stands for.

questions.q: Which types of atoms are in HCl?
questions.explain: H is the symbol for hydrogen and Cl is the symbol for chlorine. HCl contains hydrogen atoms and chlorine atoms.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: HCl contains another symbol, H, before Cl. Each different symbol stands for a different type of atom.
notes.1: The symbol for helium is He, not H. Check what H stands for.
notes.2: A symbol starts with a capital letter, and a small letter after it belongs to the same symbol. Check what Cl stands for.

questions.q: In C₆H₁₂O₆, how many carbon atoms are there?
questions.explain: In C₆H₁₂O₆, the small 6 after C shows six carbon atoms.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: The C in C₆H₁₂O₆ has a small number after it. Look at the number written straight after C.
notes.1: 12 is the number of hydrogen atoms. Look at the number written straight after C.
notes.3: 24 is the total number of atoms in the molecule. The question asks only about carbon atoms.

why.right: C₆H₁₂O₆ has six carbon atoms because the small 6 counts the atoms of the element just before it.
wrong: C₆H₁₂O₆ has six carbon atoms because the small 6 counts the atoms of the element just after it.
C₆H₁₂O₆ has six carbon atoms because the first number in a formula counts all of its atoms.

questions.q: What is the total number of atoms in one C₆H₁₂O₆ molecule?
questions.explain: C₆H₁₂O₆ has 6 carbon atoms, 12 hydrogen atoms and 6 oxygen atoms. The total is 6 + 12 + 6 = 24 atoms.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.1: 18 leaves out the atoms of one element. Add the carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms together.
notes.2: 3 is the number of types of atom, not the number of atoms. The small numbers count the atoms of each type.
notes.3: 6 is only the carbon atoms, or only the oxygen atoms. All the atoms must be added together.

why.right: C₆H₁₂O₆ has 24 atoms because the small numbers 6, 12 and 6 are added together.
wrong: C₆H₁₂O₆ has 24 atoms because every sugar molecule contains exactly 24 atoms.
C₆H₁₂O₆ has 24 atoms because each of the three types of atom is counted eight times.

questions.q: A molecule has 1 nitrogen atom and 3 hydrogen atoms. Which formula represents it?
questions.explain: One nitrogen atom is written as N with no number. Three hydrogen atoms are written as H with a small 3. This gives NH₃.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: N₃H shows 3 nitrogen atoms and 1 hydrogen atom, the wrong way round. A small number counts the symbol just before it.
notes.1: N₃H₃ shows 3 nitrogen atoms. There is only 1 nitrogen atom, and the number 1 is not written.
notes.2: NH shows only 1 hydrogen atom. The small number for hydrogen is missing.

why.right: NH₃ is the formula because a small number after a symbol counts the atoms of that element.
wrong: NH₃ is the formula because a small number at the end counts the atoms of every element.
NH₃ is the formula because the element with the most atoms is always written first.

questions.q: A molecule has 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms. Which formula represents it?
questions.explain: One carbon atom is written as C with no number. Two oxygen atoms are written as O with a small 2. This gives CO₂.
questions.lo: State the numbers and types of atoms from a chemical formula

notes.0: C₂O shows 2 carbon atoms and 1 oxygen atom, the wrong way round. A small number counts the symbol just before it.
notes.2: C₂O₂ shows 2 carbon atoms. There is only 1 carbon atom, and the number 1 is not written.
notes.3: CO shows only 1 oxygen atom. The small number for oxygen is missing.

why.right: CO₂ is the formula because a small number after a symbol counts the atoms of that element.
wrong: CO₂ is the formula because a small number at the end counts the atoms of every element.
CO₂ is the formula because the element with fewer atoms always gets the small number.

questions.q: A molecule of an element contains
choices: two or more types of atoms
questions.explain: An element is made up of only one type of atom. A molecule of an element contains two or more atoms of the same type.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: Two or more types of atom chemically combined make a compound. An element has fewer types than this.
notes.1: A molecule has two or more atoms, so it cannot be only one atom. Think about how many types of atom an element has.
notes.3: Atoms in a molecule are always chemically combined. Think about how many types of atom an element has.

questions.q: A molecule of a compound contains
choices: two or more types of atoms
questions.explain: A compound is made of two or more elements chemically combined. A molecule of a compound contains two or more types of atoms.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: Atoms in a molecule are always chemically combined. Think about how many types of atom a compound has.
notes.2: A molecule has two or more atoms, so it cannot be only one atom. Think about how many types of atom a compound has.
notes.3: Only one type of atom describes a molecule of an element. A compound is made of more than one element.

questions.q: Does O₂ represent an element or a compound?
questions.explain: O₂ contains only oxygen atoms, which is one type of atom. So O₂ represents an element.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.1: A mixture contains substances that are not chemically combined. The atoms in O₂ are chemically combined in one molecule.
notes.2: A compound needs two or more types of atom. Count how many different symbols are in O₂.

why.right: O₂ is an element because its molecule contains only one type of atom.
wrong: O₂ is an element because its molecule contains only one atom.
O₂ is an element because its molecule contains two atoms of different types.

questions.q: Does CO represent an element or a compound?
questions.explain: CO contains carbon atoms and oxygen atoms chemically combined. It has two types of atom, so it is a compound.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: The carbon and oxygen in CO are chemically combined in one molecule. A mixture has parts that are not combined.
notes.1: The capital O in CO starts a second symbol, for oxygen. Count the types of atom in the formula.

why.right: CO is a compound because its molecule contains two different types of atom chemically combined.
wrong: CO is a compound because its molecule contains only one type of atom.
CO is a compound because its carbon and oxygen are mixed but not chemically combined.

questions.q: Does S₈ represent an element or a compound?
questions.explain: S₈ contains only sulfur atoms, which is one type of atom. Even with 8 atoms combined, it is still an element.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: The sulfur atoms in S₈ are chemically combined in one molecule. A mixture has parts that are not combined.
notes.1: Having many atoms does not make a compound. A compound needs two or more types of atom.

why.right: S₈ is an element because all 8 atoms in its molecule are the same type of atom.
wrong: S₈ is an element because a molecule with more than 2 atoms is always an element.
S₈ is an element because the 8 shows that each sulfur atom has 8 protons.

questions.q: Which formula represents a molecule of a compound?
questions.explain: NH₃ contains nitrogen and hydrogen atoms chemically combined. It has two types of atom, so it is a compound. Cl₂, I₂ and N₂ each contain one type of atom.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: Cl₂ contains only chlorine atoms. A compound needs two or more types of atom.
notes.1: I₂ contains only iodine atoms. A compound needs two or more types of atom.
notes.2: N₂ contains only nitrogen atoms. A compound needs two or more types of atom.

why.right: NH₃ is a compound because its molecule contains two different types of atom chemically combined.
wrong: NH₃ is a compound because its molecule contains more than two atoms.
NH₃ is a compound because its formula contains a small number.

questions.q: Which formula represents a molecule of an element?
questions.explain: I₂ contains only iodine atoms, which is one type of atom, so it is an element. H₂O, HCl and CO₂ each contain two types of atom.
questions.lo: Classify a molecule as an element or a compound from its formula

notes.0: H₂O contains hydrogen and oxygen atoms. Two types of atom chemically combined make a compound.
notes.2: HCl contains hydrogen and chlorine atoms. Two types of atom chemically combined make a compound.
notes.3: CO₂ contains carbon and oxygen atoms. Two types of atom chemically combined make a compound.

why.right: I₂ is an element because its molecule contains only one type of atom.
wrong: I₂ is an element because its molecule contains exactly two atoms.
I₂ is an element because its molecule has the shortest formula.

questions.q: Which statement about atoms and molecules is correct?
choices: atoms and molecules are the same
atoms are made up of molecules
molecules are made up of atoms
questions.explain: Molecules are made up of two or more atoms chemically combined. Atoms are the smaller units that build up molecules.
questions.lo: Compare atoms and molecules

notes.0: An atom is a single unit, while a molecule is a group of atoms joined together. They are not the same.
notes.1: A molecule is built from atoms, so it is not smaller than the atoms it contains.
notes.2: Atoms are made of protons, neutrons and electrons, not molecules. Think about which is the smaller unit.

why.right: Molecules are made up of atoms because a molecule is two or more atoms chemically combined.
wrong: Molecules are made up of atoms because an atom is two or more molecules chemically combined.
Molecules are made up of atoms because atoms and molecules are two names for the same thing.

questions.q: How is a hydrogen molecule different from a hydrogen atom?
choices: it has two hydrogen atoms combined
it has different types of atoms
questions.explain: A hydrogen atom is a single atom. A hydrogen molecule, H₂, has two hydrogen atoms chemically combined. Both contain only hydrogen.
questions.lo: Compare atoms and molecules

notes.1: A hydrogen molecule is made of hydrogen atoms, which each have an electron. Joining the atoms does not remove their electrons.
notes.2: A hydrogen molecule contains only hydrogen atoms, so it is still the same element.
notes.3: A hydrogen molecule contains only one type of atom. Think about how many atoms it has.

why.right: A hydrogen molecule differs from a hydrogen atom because it is two hydrogen atoms chemically combined.
wrong: A hydrogen molecule differs from a hydrogen atom because it contains a different element.
A hydrogen molecule differs from a hydrogen atom because its atoms have lost their electrons.

questions.q: Based on the planetary model, an atom is mostly
questions.explain: In the planetary model, the nucleus is tiny and the electrons move around it at a large distance. Most of the atom is empty space.
questions.lo: Describe how atomic models are simplified and revised with new evidence

notes.0: Protons are packed into the tiny nucleus at the centre. Think about what fills most of the atom around the nucleus.
notes.1: Neutrons are packed into the tiny nucleus at the centre. Think about what fills most of the atom around the nucleus.
notes.3: Electrons are very small and take up very little room. Think about what lies between the electrons and the nucleus.

why.right: An atom is mostly empty space because its tiny nucleus is far from the electrons moving around it.
wrong: An atom is mostly empty space because its electrons are spread out to fill the whole atom.
An atom is mostly empty space because its protons and neutrons are spread through the atom.

questions.q: Why were older models of the atom replaced?
choices: they were too hard to draw
they could not explain many properties of atoms
questions.explain: Older models of the atom were replaced because they could not explain many properties of atoms. Scientists revised the models when new evidence was found.
questions.lo: Describe how atomic models are simplified and revised with new evidence

notes.0: Science does not change models because people dislike them. Models change when they do not match the evidence.
notes.1: How hard a model is to draw does not decide whether it is kept. Models change when they do not match the evidence.
notes.2: Age alone does not make a model wrong. Some old ideas are still used today because they match the evidence.

why.right: Models of the atom are replaced when new evidence shows they cannot explain what atoms do.
wrong: Models of the atom are replaced every few years so that textbooks stay up to date.
Models of the atom are replaced when most people vote that they prefer a different model.

questions.q: Atoms are drawn as coloured circles. Which is a limitation of this model?
questions.explain: Real atoms have no colour. The colours in the model are only used to tell different types of atoms apart, so this is a limitation of the model.
questions.lo: Describe how atomic models are simplified and revised with new evidence

notes.1: Atoms do combine to form molecules, and the circle model can show this. A limitation is something the model shows wrongly.
notes.2: Atoms are not larger than the molecules they make up. A limitation is something about the drawing that is not true of real atoms.
notes.3: Atoms in a model can be labelled with their symbols. A limitation is something about the drawing that is not true of real atoms.

why.right: Coloured circles are a limitation of atom models because real atoms are far too small to have colour.
wrong: Coloured circles are a limitation of atom models because real atoms are square, not round.
Coloured circles are a limitation of atom models because real atoms are all the same colour.

questions.q: Which is a medical use of atomic technology?
choices: chalk to improve a climber's grip
a beam balance to measure mass
questions.explain: X-ray imaging uses technology based on atoms to make pictures of the bones inside the body. It helps doctors find broken bones.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.0: Burning fuel is a chemical reaction used for heating, not a medical use. Look for a use in medicine.
notes.2: Chalk on a climber's hands is not medical and does not use atomic technology. Look for a use in medicine.
notes.3: A beam balance is a measuring tool, not a medical use of atomic technology. Look for a use in medicine.

questions.q: Nuclear power plants generate electricity using energy from
questions.explain: Nuclear power plants use energy released from the nuclei of atoms such as uranium. This energy heats water to make steam, which turns turbines to generate electricity.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.1: Sunlight is used by solar panels, not nuclear power plants. The word nuclear refers to the centre of an atom.
notes.2: Moving water is used in hydroelectric power plants. The word nuclear refers to the centre of an atom.
notes.3: Burning oil is used in some power stations, but not in nuclear ones. The word nuclear refers to the centre of an atom.

questions.q: Which is a risk of using nuclear power plants?
choices: accidents causing pollution and loss of life
questions.explain: Accidents at nuclear power plants can release harmful radioactive substances. These can pollute the environment and cause loss of life.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.0: Nuclear power plants produce a large amount of heat. Think about what could go wrong if something fails.
notes.2: Nuclear power plants do not use oil. Think about what could go wrong if something fails.
notes.3: Nuclear power plants do not need sunlight. Think about what could go wrong if something fails.

why.right: Nuclear power plants carry a risk because an accident can release harmful radioactive substances into the environment.
wrong: Nuclear power plants carry a risk because they burn large amounts of oil that may run out.
Nuclear power plants carry a risk because they stop working whenever there is no sunlight.

questions.q: "Should atomic bombs ever be used in war?" Which issue is this?
questions.explain: An ethical issue asks whether something is right or wrong. Asking whether atomic bombs should ever be used in war is a question of right and wrong.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.0: An environmental issue is about effects on nature and living things. This question asks whether an action is right or wrong.
notes.1: An economic issue is about money and cost. This question asks whether an action is right or wrong.

why.right: Asking whether atomic bombs should be used is an ethical issue because it is about right and wrong.
wrong: Asking whether atomic bombs should be used is an ethical issue because it is about the cost of bombs.
Asking whether atomic bombs should be used is an ethical issue because it is about damage to soil.

questions.q: "How much does it cost to build a nuclear power plant?" Which issue is this?
questions.explain: An economic issue is about money and cost. The cost of building a nuclear power plant is an economic issue.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.0: An environmental issue is about effects on nature and living things. This question is about cost.
notes.1: A social issue is about effects on people and communities. This question is about cost.
notes.2: An ethical issue asks whether something is right or wrong. This question is about cost.

why.right: The cost of building a nuclear plant is an economic issue because it is about money.
wrong: The cost of building a nuclear plant is an economic issue because it is about right and wrong.
The cost of building a nuclear plant is an economic issue because it is about harm to nature.

questions.q: A country has no oil. Why might it choose nuclear energy?
choices: it produces no waste at all
it carries no risk of accidents
it can generate electricity without oil
questions.explain: Nuclear power plants use energy from atoms such as uranium instead of oil. A country without oil can still generate electricity this way.
questions.lo: Identify applications of atomic technologies and the issues and risks they raise

notes.0: Nuclear power plants do produce waste, and some of it is radioactive. Think about what a country without oil needs.
notes.1: Nuclear power plants do carry a risk of accidents. Think about what a country without oil needs.
notes.3: Nuclear power plants use steam to turn turbines. Think about what a country without oil needs.

why.right: A country without oil might use nuclear energy because nuclear plants use uranium instead of oil as fuel.
wrong: A country without oil might use nuclear energy because nuclear plants produce no waste of any kind.
A country without oil might use nuclear energy because nuclear plants can never have accidents.
